text.p: ACTV Inc president William Samuels said ACTV and partner Fox Sports Southwest plan to begin offering later this year in selected regions around the U.S. a form of interactive television geared to hardcore sports fans. Or at least those with a penchant for toying with remote controls.
Fox Sports Southwest is a unit of Fox Sports Net -- an alliance of News Corp Ltd, Tele-Communications Inc and Tele-Communications' Liberty Media Corp affiliate.

Using a digital cable television box and a special, four-button remote, a subscriber of the premium cable channel will be able to call up player statistics and interviews, activate instant replays and focus on star players while watching sporting events.

Samuels said in an interview with Reuters that the company expects the service to cost about $9.95 per month and to reach as many as 50,000 subscribers in the first year in each of its first two regions. The company hopes to launch the service in two regions by the end of the year and to announce a third region by the end of this year.

The first region, which was announced this week, is part of Texas. The other is widely expected to be in the Los Angeles area, where the company has been conducting a one-year test in the Ventura County, Calif., area served by Tele-Communications Inc's cable system.

"The underlying concept is the individualization of programming," Samuels said. "Sports is the anchor. Sports is what will drive it." Samuels said the company hopes to reach a 10 percent market penetration rate within five years.
It remains to be seen whether the venture will be able to live up to those expectations.
"There's a market for it but it's going to take time to develop," said John Mansell, a senior analyst at Paul Kagan Associates.
"Who knows? I guess it's sort of a wet-finger-in-the-air approach right now," said Michael Shonstrom, an analyst with Neidiger Tucker Bruner Inc.
With 100,000 subscribers, the venture would generate about $6 million in revenues, which could be supplemented by between 10 percent and 25 percent with advertising, Shonstrom said.
H.J. Meyers & Co analyst Peter Mintz said he expected it would take between three and 12 months' operation to generate a one percent penetration of the market.
Mintz projects a three percent penetration rate within two years and five percent in the third year. The market would be considered saturated at 10 percent, he said.
There are several hurdles to be overcome.
The concentration of sports programming and the necessity to frequently use the remote is said to appeal more to male viewers than women, Samuels said.
"The research showed a real gender gap vis-a-vis programming," he said.

ACTV is hoping to assuage women viewers who are not interested in watching sports by also offering educational programming and news. The service is likely to begin with a minimum of eight hours and a maximum of 12 hours on-air time, Samuels said.
Its partner in the venture, Fox Sports Southwest, provides coverage to about five million cable and satellite television homes in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and parts of New Mexico.
